mainTopic: Which materials count as an אֹהֶל for טומאת מת, whether the תחש was kosher, and finding a source that non-kosher hide becomes טמא in an אהל המת
overview: This עמוד first finishes proving that linen counts as an אֹהֶל for טומאת מת, through a גזירה שוה from the משכן. The גמרא then tests the limits of that comparison. A רִבּוּי removes the need for six-fold twisted thread, the beams (קרשים) are excluded, and the hide coverings are included through a היקש. Next it examines רבי אלעזר's question about the hide of a non-kosher animal. רב אדא בר אהבה explains that the doubt is whether the תחש was kosher. רב יוסף shows that it was kosher, reading רבי נחמיה's comparison to the תלא אילן as being only about its colors. רבא then tries to prove that non-kosher hide becomes טמא in an אהל המת. Proofs from נגעים alone and from שרצים alone are each refuted, so the גמרא combines them into a צד השוה. רבא מברניש refutes that too, since both spread טומאה with less than a כזית. He begins his own source, which continues on the next עמוד.

steps.title: Linen counts as a tent: learned from the Tabernacle
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes its answer that linen is called אֹהֶל, using a גזירה שוה between the אֹהֶל of טומאת מת and the אֹהֶל of the משכן.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learn it from the משכן. Here it says 'This is the law: when a man dies in a tent,' and there it says 'And he spread the tent over the משכן.' The tent of the משכן was linen and is called a tent. So here too, linen is called a tent.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא completes its answer to the earlier question of how we know linen counts as an אֹהֶל. It links the two places where the Torah uses the word אֹהֶל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word אֹהֶל appears in the laws of טומאת מת and also by the משכן. Since the משכן's tent was made of linen, a גזירה שוה teaches that linen is the material the Torah calls an אֹהֶל. This sets the base rule that the rest of this passage will test and refine.

keyTerms.meaning: Tent; a covering that spreads טומאת מת to what is under it
'It is written here... and it is written there': the formula of a גזירה שוה
'Just as there... so too here': the comparison step

steps.confusionAlert: The first word 'מִמִּשְׁכָּן' finishes a sentence from the previous עמוד, which asked how we know linen is called אֹהֶל. It is not a new topic.

phrases.english: from the Tabernacle.
phrases.notes: Completes the answer begun on 27b: we learn 'tent' 'tent' from the משכן.

phrases.english: It is written here: "This is the law
when a man dies in a tent",
and it is written there:
"And he spread the tent over the Tabernacle."
Just as there, linen is called a "tent,"
so too here, linen is called a "tent."

steps.triggerLanguage: כְּתִיב הָכָא: זֹאת הַתּוֹרָה אָדָם כִּי יָמוּת בְּאֹהֶל, וּכְתִיב הָתָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the answer to the question asked on the previous עמוד
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A גזירה שוה of אֹהֶל אֹהֶל from the משכן shows that linen is called אֹהֶל
steps.whyThisMatters: Every challenge that follows tests how far this גזירה שוה comparison can be pushed.

steps.title: Must the linen be twisted and six-fold like the Tabernacle's?
steps.stepSummary: If we compare to the משכן, maybe we must copy every detail, including twisted six-fold threads.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, just as there the threads were twisted and doubled six times, should it be the same here?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the comparison. If we learn from the משכן, maybe only linen exactly like the משכן's counts.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A comparison usually carries the details of the source along with it. The משכן's linen was שזור, with threads folded six times. Ordinary linen tents are not made that way, so this would greatly narrow the rule.

phrases.english: If so: just as there the threads are twisted
and their thread is folded six times,
so too here they must be twisted
and their thread folded six times?

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי מַה לְּהַלָּן שְׁזוּרִין וְחוּטָן כָּפוּל שִׁשָּׁה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Pushes the גזירה שוה to require all the details of the משכן
steps.kashyaTarget: The scope of the גזירה שוה in step 1
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the comparison is full, it should require every detail of the משכן's linen

steps.title: The repeated word 'tent' widens the rule
steps.stepSummary: The Torah repeats אֹהֶל several times, which is a רִבּוּי that includes any linen.
steps.simpleTranslation: The verse says 'tent,' 'tent' many times, which comes to include more.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the Torah's repetition of the word אֹהֶל widens the rule. So simple linen also counts, not only six-fold twisted linen.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the פרשה of טומאת מת, the word אֹהֶל appears again and again. That extra wording is read as a רִבּוּי (an inclusion). It removes the need to copy the משכן's special thread details.

keyTerms.meaning: 'The verse teaches': introducing a proof from a פסוק

phrases.english: The verse states:
"tent," "tent": it amplified (to include more).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the six-fold thread challenge
steps.terutzResolutionType: Additional textual inclusion (רִבּוּי) limits the detail-copying of the גזירה שוה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Only linen exactly like the משכן's would count
steps.terutzMaskana: Any linen counts, because of the repeated word אֹהֶל

steps.title: Then let the widening include every material
steps.stepSummary: If the repetition widens, why stop at linen? Let everything count as an אֹהֶל.
steps.simpleTranslation: If 'tent, tent' widens the rule, then everything should be included too!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer. If the רִבּוּי widens the rule, it could include every material, not only linen.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A רִבּוּי has no built-in stopping point. If it can include ordinary linen, perhaps it includes wool, leather, wood, and everything else.

phrases.english: If "tent," "tent" amplifies,
then even all things should be included too!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי אֹהֶל אֹהֶל רִיבָּה, אֲפִילּוּ כׇּל מִילֵּי נָמֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the רִבּוּי from step 3 as too broad
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: An unlimited inclusion would make every material an אֹהֶל

steps.title: Otherwise the comparison would be pointless
steps.stepSummary: If everything were included, the גזירה שוה would teach nothing. So the comparison limits the רִבּוּי to linen.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, what would the גזירה שוה be good for?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the רִבּוּי cannot include everything. If it did, the גזירה שוה would have no purpose.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The two tools work together. The גזירה שוה limits the material to linen, and the רִבּוּי drops the special thread requirements. Neither cancels the other.

keyTerms.meaning: A comparison between two places that use the same word

steps.whatToRemember: Linen counts as an אֹהֶל. The גזירה שוה sets the material as linen, and the רִבּוּי of אֹהֶל אֹהֶל removes the need for twisted six-fold threads.

phrases.english: If so, the verbal analogy,
what purpose does it serve?!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִם כֵּן גְּזֵירָה שָׁוָה מַאי אַהֲנִי לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 4 by pointing to the purpose of the גזירה שוה
steps.terutzResolutionType: Each derivation limits the other so that neither is wasted
steps.terutzMaskana: Only linen is included, but without the משכן's thread details

steps.title: Should beams count as a tent too?
steps.stepSummary: The משכן also had קרשים (beams), so maybe beams should count as an אֹהֶל.
steps.simpleTranslation: But say: just as there were beams there, so too beams here!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries another comparison. The משכן had wooden beams, so maybe beams also count as an אֹהֶל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the משכן is the model for what an אֹהֶל is, its wooden beams might be part of that model too. That would add wood as a material.

keyTerms.meaning: The wooden beams of the משכן

phrases.english: But say: just as there were beams there,
so too here, beams!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאֵימָא: מַה לְּהַלָּן קְרָשִׁים, אַף כָּאן קְרָשִׁים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new challenge to the scope of the משכן comparison
steps.kashyaTarget: The limiting of אֹהֶל to linen
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משכן included wooden beams, so wood should also be an אֹהֶל

steps.title: The beams are not called the Tabernacle
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק says 'beams for the משכן,' which shows the beams are separate from the משכן itself.
steps.simpleTranslation: The verse says, 'Make beams for the משכן.' The משכן is called משכן, but the beams are not called משכן.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers from the wording of a פסוק. The beams are made 'for' the משכן, so they are not the משכן itself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'for' (לַמִּשְׁכָּן) shows that the beams only serve the משכן. Only the curtains carry the name, so only they serve as the model for an אֹהֶל.

phrases.english: The verse said:
"And you shall make the beams for the Tabernacle."
The Tabernacle (the curtains) is called Tabernacle,
but the beams are not called Tabernacle.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the beams challenge
steps.terutzResolutionType: Precise reading of the פסוק separates the beams from the משכן
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Beams are part of the משכן and so count as an אֹהֶל
steps.terutzMaskana: Beams serve the משכן but are not called משכן

steps.title: By that logic, the covering is not a tent either
steps.stepSummary: The same reasoning applied to 'a covering for the tent' would mean the hide covering is not an אֹהֶל.
steps.simpleTranslation: But if so: 'Make a covering for the tent.' Then here too, the covering would not be called a tent.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns the same reading method against the answer. A similar פסוק says the covering is 'for the tent.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: If 'for the משכן' excludes the beams, then 'for the tent' should exclude the hide coverings from being called אֹהֶל. This step sets up the problem stated in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: 'But if so, from now on': applying a logic to reach a problem
Covering (the hide layer over the משכן)

phrases.english: But if that is so,
"And you shall make a covering for the tent":
so too, the covering would not be called a "tent."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies step 7's reading method to the hide coverings
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The same wording pattern would exclude the coverings from being an אֹהֶל

steps.title: Then רבי אלעזר's question makes no sense
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר asked whether non-kosher hide becomes טמא as an אֹהֶל. If even kosher hide does not, his question is pointless.
steps.simpleTranslation: But then, what about רבי אלעזר's question: can the hide of a non-kosher animal become טמא in an אֹהֶל המת? Now, if even the hide of a kosher animal does not become טמא, is there any question about the hide of a non-kosher animal?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows why step 8 is a real problem. If hide coverings are not an אֹהֶל, then רבי אלעזר's question would make no sense.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אלעזר only questioned non-kosher hide. That implies kosher hide definitely counts as an אֹהֶל. Step 8's logic would deny this even for kosher hide, which would leave רבי אלעזר's question with no point.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Now if [the stronger case]... is there a question [about the weaker]?'

phrases.english: But then, what about the question Rabbi Elazar raised:
the hide of a non-kosher animal,
what is the law: does it become impure as a tent over a corpse?

phrases.aramaic: הַשְׁתָּא עוֹר בְּהֵמָה טְהוֹרָה לָא מִטַּמֵּא,
phrases.english: Now, if the hide of a kosher animal does not become impure,
is there a question about the hide of a non-kosher animal?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows the contradiction that step 8 creates
steps.kashyaTarget: The conclusion that the hide covering is not an אֹהֶל
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי אלעזר's question assumes kosher hide is an אֹהֶל. Step 8's logic would make his question pointless.

steps.title: A later verse joins the covering to the tent
steps.stepSummary: Another פסוק lists the coverings together with the אֹהֶל, a היקש that gives the upper covering the status of אֹהֶל.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is different there, because the verse went back and included it. It is written: 'They shall carry the curtains of the משכן, and the אהל מועד, its covering, and the covering of תחש that is on it.' The verse compares the upper to the lower: just as the lower is called a tent, so too the upper is called a tent.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the coverings are a special case. Another פסוק puts them back together with the אֹהֶל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By itself, 'a covering for the tent' would exclude the coverings. But a later פסוק lists them side by side with the אֹהֶל, making a היקש. So the hides are also an אֹהֶל, while the beams stay excluded.

keyTerms.meaning: The verse went back and restored it
Compares by placing side by side (היקש)
The upper (hide) layer / the lower (linen) layer

steps.whatToRemember: Linen curtains and the hide coverings count as אֹהֶל, but the beams do not. The hides are included only because of the היקש in a later פסוק.

phrases.english: It is different there,
because the verse went back and restored it,
as it is written: "And they shall carry the curtains of the Tabernacle,
and the Tent of Meeting, its covering,
and the covering of tachash that is upon it."
It compares the upper to the lower:
just as the lower is called a "tent,"
so too the upper is called a "tent."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers steps 8 and 9 by treating the coverings as an exception
steps.terutzResolutionType: A separate פסוק creates a היקש for the coverings
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The covering is excluded just like the beams
steps.terutzMaskana: The coverings are an אֹהֶל because of the היקש. The beams remain excluded.

steps.title: רבי אלעזר's question, studied directly
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא returns to examine רבי אלעזר's question on its own: does non-kosher hide become טמא as an אֹהֶל?
steps.simpleTranslation: The matter itself: רבי אלעזר asked, can the hide of a non-kosher animal become טמא with טומאת אהלים?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now studies רבי אלעזר's question for its own sake. This step sets up the analysis that follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Until now the question was only used as a tool in the argument. The word גּוּפָא signals that the גמרא will now explain what the question really means.

keyTerms.meaning: 'The matter itself': returning to discuss a statement quoted earlier
Impurity of tents (as an אֹהֶל over a מת)

phrases.english: The matter itself:
Rabbi Elazar raised a question:
the hide of a non-kosher animal,
what is the law: does it become impure with the impurity of tents?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to a statement quoted in step 9 in order to examine it
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An open question: is non-kosher hide an אֹהֶל for טומאה?

steps.title: What exactly was his doubt?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the basis of רבי אלעזר's doubt was.
steps.simpleTranslation: What was he unsure about?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what was behind רבי אלעזר's question. This sets up the explanation in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the hides count as אֹהֶל through the היקש, the גמרא wants to know why non-kosher hide would be any different.

phrases.english: What was his question about?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reason behind step 11
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The basis of רבי אלעזר's doubt

steps.title: Was the תחש kosher or not?
steps.stepSummary: רב אדא בר אהבה explains that the doubt is whether the תחש of משה's time was kosher.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אדא בר אהבה said: he was asking about the תחש of משה's time. Was it non-kosher or kosher?
steps.whatsHappening: רב אדא בר אהבה explains that the doubt is really a factual question about the תחש animal.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The hide coverings are an אֹהֶל because of the היקש. If the תחש was non-kosher, then non-kosher hide would also be included. So the question depends on the identity of the תחש.

keyTerms.meaning: The animal whose hide covered the משכן

phrases.english: Rav Adda bar Ahava said:

phrases.aramaic: תַּחַשׁ שֶׁהָיָה בִּימֵי מֹשֶׁה קָמִיבַּעְיָא לֵיהּ —
phrases.english: he was asking about the tachash that existed in the days of Moshe:
was it non-kosher or was it kosher?

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב אַדָּא בַּר אַהֲבָה: תַּחַשׁ שֶׁהָיָה בִּימֵי מֹשֶׁה קָמִיבַּעְיָא לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 12
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The doubt is whether the תחש was a kosher or non-kosher animal

steps.title: רב יוסף: only kosher hides were used
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף asks why there is any doubt, since a ברייתא teaches that only kosher hide was fit for holy work.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said: why should he be unsure? We learned: only the hide of a kosher animal was fit for heavenly work!
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף challenges the doubt. A ברייתא already says that only kosher hides were used in holy work, so the תחש must have been kosher.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If only kosher hides were allowed in the משכן, the תחש must have been kosher. So the משכן cannot be the source for including non-kosher hide, and רב אדא בר אהבה's explanation of the doubt seems to have no basis.

phrases.english: Rav Yosef said:
Why should he be unsure?
We learned: nothing was made fit for heavenly work
except the hide of a kosher animal alone!

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יוֹסֵף: מַאי תִּיבְּעֵי לֵיהּ, תְּנֵינָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the doubt explained in step 13
steps.kashyaTarget: The doubt about whether the תחש was kosher
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא rules that only kosher hide was used, so the תחש must have been kosher

steps.title: רבי אבא: the תחש was like the non-kosher תלא אילן
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבא objects from a ברייתא where רבי נחמיה compares the תחש to the תלא אילן, a non-kosher animal.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבא objected: רבי יהודה says there were two coverings, one of red ram skins and one of תחש skins. רבי נחמיה says there was one covering, and it looked like a תלא אילן. But the תלא אילן is non-kosher!
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אבא challenges רב יוסף from a ברייתא. רבי נחמיה compared the תחש to the תלא אילן, which is non-kosher.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא first brings the disagreement about how many coverings there were. The objection comes from רבי נחמיה's comparison of the תחש to a non-kosher animal. This suggests the תחש was non-kosher, against רב יוסף's claim.

phrases.english: Rabbi Abba raised an objection:

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: שְׁנֵי מִכְסָאוֹת הָיוּ,
phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says: there were two coverings,
one of reddened rams' skins
and one of tachash skins.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי נְחֶמְיָה אוֹמֵר: מִכְסֶה אֶחָד הָיָה,
phrases.english: Rabbi Nechemya says: there was one covering,
and it resembled a kind of tela ilan.
But the tela ilan is non-kosher!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Objects to רב יוסף's claim in step 14
steps.kashyaTarget: רב יוסף's claim that the תחש was kosher
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי נחמיה compares the תחש to the non-kosher תלא אילן

steps.title: Similar only in its colors
steps.stepSummary: רבי נחמיה meant the תחש was multicolored like the תלא אילן, but it was a different, kosher animal.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what he meant: it was like a תלא אילן in that it had many colors, but it was not a תלא אילן. The תלא אילן is non-kosher, but this one was kosher.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains that רבי נחמיה's comparison was only about appearance, not about the animal's species.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Like a תלא אילן' means it shared the many colors. It does not mean it was the same animal. So the תחש can still be kosher, and רב יוסף's position stands.

keyTerms.meaning: 'This is what he meant': reinterpreting a statement

phrases.english: This is what he meant:
it is like a tela ilan,
in that it has many colors,
but it is not a tela ilan.
For there, it is non-kosher,
and here, it is kosher.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָכִי קָאָמַר: כְּמִין תְּלָא אִילָן הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבי אבא's objection
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterprets the comparison as about appearance only
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The תחש was a תלא אילן, a non-kosher animal
steps.terutzMaskana: The תחש only looked like the תלא אילן and was kosher

steps.title: The תרגום 'ססגונא' fits this
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף supports the answer: the תרגום calls the תחש 'ססגונא,' meaning it rejoices in many colors.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said: if so, that is why we translate it 'ססגונא,' because it rejoices in many colors.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף adds support for the answer. The Aramaic תרגום name for the תחש itself refers to its many colors.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'ססגונא' is read as שָׂשׂ (rejoices) plus גְּווֹנִין (colors). This confirms that the תחש was known for its colors, which fits the reading that it was a kosher, multicolored animal.

keyTerms.meaning: The תרגום's name for תחש: 'rejoicing in colors'

steps.whatToRemember: According to רב יוסף, the תחש was a kosher, multicolored animal, and only kosher hides were used in the משכן. רבי נחמיה's comparison to the תלא אילן refers only to its colors.

phrases.english: Rav Yosef said:
If so, that is why we translate it "sasgona,"
because it rejoices in many colors.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יוֹסֵף: אִי הָכִי הַיְינוּ דִּמְתַרְגְּמִינַן סָסְגּוֹנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the answer in step 16
steps.raayaObject: That the תחש was described by its many colors (and so could be a kosher animal)

steps.title: רבא learns it from the laws of צרעת
steps.stepSummary: רבא brings a ברייתא showing that in נגעים, the extra words 'או בעור' include non-kosher hide. He wants to learn from this that non-kosher hide is also טמא in an אהל המת.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: we know that hide of a non-kosher animal becomes טמא in a tent with a dead body from here. A ברייתא teaches: the verse could have said 'hide,' but it says 'or in a hide.' This extra wording includes hide of a non-kosher animal, and hide that became afflicted while in the כהן's hands. And if someone cut pieces from all of these and made one item out of them, how do we know it is included? The verse says: 'or in anything made of hide.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives a first source for our question. He points to the laws of נגעים, where the Torah clearly includes non-kosher hide.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the פרשה of נגעים, the extra words 'או בעור' teach that non-kosher hide can become טמא. רבא's idea is to carry this rule over to אהל המת: if non-kosher hide counts as 'hide' for נגעים, it should count as 'hide' for a tent over a dead body too.

keyTerms.meaning: That became afflicted while it was in the hands of the כהן
He cut pieces from all of them

phrases.english: Rava said:

phrases.aramaic: עוֹר בְּהֵמָה טְמֵאָה דְּמִטַּמֵּא בְּאֹהֶל הַמֵּת
phrases.english: that hide of a non-kosher animal becomes impure in a tent of a corpse
is learned from here, as it was taught in a baraita:
'Hide' — the verse says 'or in a hide' —
phrases.notes: The extra wording is read as an inclusion.

phrases.english: it included hide of a non-kosher animal,
and hide that became afflicted in the hand of the priest.

phrases.aramaic: קָצַץ מִכּוּלָּן וְעָשָׂה אַחַת מֵהֶן, מִנַּיִן? —
phrases.english: If he cut from all of them and made one item from them, from where do we know?
The verse says: 'or in anything made of hide.'

steps.triggerLanguage: רָבָא אָמַר: עוֹר בְּהֵמָה טְמֵאָה דְּמִטַּמֵּא בְּאֹהֶל הַמֵּת מֵהָכָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the side discussion about the תחש, the גמרא returns to finding a source for non-kosher hide in an אהל המת.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Non-kosher hide is included for נגעים through 'או בעור', and רבא proposes learning אהל המת from this.

steps.title: צרעת is stricter, so we cannot learn from it
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects learning from נגעים. נגעים are stricter, because even loose threads (שתי וערב) become טמא there.
steps.simpleTranslation: But this can be refuted: what about נגעים? They are special, because even warp and woof threads become טמא with them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes away רבא's proof from נגעים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: You cannot learn a rule from a stricter area of law and apply it to a less strict one. In נגעים, even plain threads that are not yet woven into cloth can become טמא, which shows that נגעים are unusually strict. So including non-kosher hide there may also be part of that strictness, and it tells us nothing about אהל המת.

keyTerms.meaning: There is room to refute (the comparison)
Warp and woof threads, not yet woven into a garment

phrases.english: But there is room to refute:
what about leprous afflictions?
For with them even warp and woof threads become impure.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the source offered in step 18.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The whole derivation from נגעים alone.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: נגעים have an extra strictness (שתי וערב), so their rules cannot be applied to the milder אהל המת.

steps.title: Trying to learn it from שרצים instead
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests learning it from שרצים instead. There, too, 'או עור' includes non-kosher hide.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, he learned it from שרצים. A ברייתא teaches: 'hide' — from this I only know about hide of a kosher animal. How do we know about hide of a non-kosher animal? The verse says 'or hide.'
steps.whatsHappening: Since נגעים did not work, the גמרא offers a different source: the laws of שרצים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the פרשה of שרצים, the extra 'או עור' includes non-kosher hide for becoming טמא through touching a שרץ. The suggestion is to learn אהל המת from this instead of from נגעים.

keyTerms.meaning: He learned it from the laws of creeping creatures
I would only know (that the basic case is included)

phrases.english: Rather, he learned it from creeping creatures,
as it was taught in a baraita: 'Hide' —

phrases.aramaic: אֵין לִי אֶלָּא עוֹר בְּהֵמָה טְהוֹרָה,
phrases.english: I only know about hide of a kosher animal.
From where do we know about hide of a non-kosher animal?
The verse says: 'or hide.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the rejected source from נגעים with a new source from שרצים.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The rule must come from נגעים, which was refuted.
steps.terutzMaskana: It can come from שרצים, where non-kosher hide is also included.

steps.title: שרצים are stricter too
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects learning from שרצים. A שרץ makes things טמא at only a lentil's size, which is stricter than a מת.
steps.simpleTranslation: But this can be refuted: what about שרצים? They are special, because they make things טמא at the size of a lentil.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes away the proof from שרצים, just as it pushed away the proof from נגעים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A tiny piece of a שרץ, only כעדשה, already spreads טומאה. A מת needs at least a כזית, so שרצים are stricter. Their strictness might be the reason non-kosher hide is included there.

phrases.english: But there is room to refute:
what about creeping creatures?
For they make things impure at the size of a lentil.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the source offered in step 20.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: שרצים are stricter because they spread טומאה at a lentil's size, while a מת needs a כזית.

steps.title: צרעת proves the lentil-size point does not matter
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that נגעים prove the point. נגעים do not spread טומאה at a lentil's size, yet non-kosher hide is still included there.
steps.simpleTranslation: נגעים will prove it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the objection about lentil size by pointing back to נגעים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A נגע has to be bigger than a lentil (the size of a גריס), so נגעים lack the 'lentil' strictness of שרצים. Even so, non-kosher hide becomes טמא in נגעים. This shows that the lentil-size strictness is not the reason non-kosher hide is included.

keyTerms.meaning: Will prove (a case that disproves the claimed reason)

phrases.english: Leprous afflictions will prove it.
phrases.notes: נגעים do not spread טומאה at lentil size, yet non-kosher hide is included.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the objection of step 21 by using the source that was rejected in step 19.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The lentil-size strictness explains why non-kosher hide is included in שרצים.
steps.terutzMaskana: נגעים lack that strictness and still include non-kosher hide, so lentil size is not the reason.

steps.title: Building the rule from what both cases share
steps.stepSummary: Each case has its own weakness, but they share one feature: hide becomes טמא in both, and non-kosher hide is treated like kosher hide. The same should apply to אהל המת.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the reasoning goes back and forth. This case is not like that case, and that case is not like this case. What they share is that hide becomes טמא in both of them, and the Torah made non-kosher hide like kosher hide. So I will also bring אהל המת, where hide becomes טמא, and treat non-kosher hide there like kosher hide.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא combines נגעים and שרצים into one proof, called a צד השוה. Each one covers the other's weakness.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The objection to נגעים (the threads) does not apply to שרצים. The objection to שרצים (lentil size) does not apply to נגעים. Since neither special strictness is shared by both, the rule must come from what they do share: hide becomes טמא, and non-kosher hide counts as hide. אהל המת also has hide becoming טמא, so it should follow the same rule.

keyTerms.meaning: The reasoning comes back around (each case answers the other)
The feature of this case is not like the feature of that case
The common feature shared by both cases

steps.whatToRemember: A צד השוה works by joining two sources that each have their own unique strictness. If the strictness of one is missing in the other, only their shared feature can be the reason for the rule.

phrases.english: And the reasoning has come back around:
the feature of this is not like the feature of that,
and the feature of that is not like the feature of this.
The common feature between them is
that hide becomes impure in them,

phrases.aramaic: וְעָשָׂה עוֹר בְּהֵמָה טְמֵאָה כְּעוֹר בְּהֵמָה טְהוֹרָה.
phrases.english: and the Torah made hide of a non-kosher animal like hide of a kosher animal.
So I too will bring the tent of a corpse,
in which hide becomes impure,
and in it we will treat hide of a non-kosher animal
like hide of a kosher animal.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְחָזַר הַדִּין, לֹא רְאִי זֶה כִּרְאִי זֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the combined derivation that step 22 made possible.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Through a צד השוה of נגעים and שרצים, non-kosher hide in an אהל המת is treated like kosher hide (pending challenge).
steps.raayaObject: That the hide of a non-kosher animal is treated like kosher hide for אהל המת.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A צד השוה combining the rules of נגעים and שרצים.

steps.title: רבא from Barnish: both cases are stricter than a corpse
steps.stepSummary: רבא מברניש tells רב אשי that the צד השוה fails. Both נגעים and שרצים spread טומאה with less than a כזית, but a מת needs a full כזית.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא מברניש said to רב אשי: this can be refuted. What about the shared feature of these two? They both make things טמא with less than an olive's size. Can you say the same about a מת, which only makes things טמא with an olive's size?
steps.whatsHappening: A new challenge attacks the combined proof itself. It finds a strictness that both sources share.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A צד השוה only works if the two sources do not share any strictness that the new case lacks. Here they do: a שרץ needs only a lentil, and a נגע only a גריס, which is also less than a כזית. A מת needs a כזית, so it is milder than both, and the derivation collapses.

keyTerms.meaning: רבא from the town of Barnish (a different אמורא from רבא)
Less than the size of an olive
Can you say (the same about the new case)?

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up רבא (who gave the derivation) with רבא מברניש (who attacks it). They are two different people.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רָבָא מִבַּרְנִישׁ לְרַב אָשֵׁי:
phrases.english: Rava from Barnish said to Rav Ashi:
There is room to refute:
what about their common feature?
For they transmit impurity with less than an olive-bulk.
Can you say the same about a corpse,
which only transmits impurity with an olive-bulk?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רָבָא מִבַּרְנִישׁ לְרַב אָשֵׁי: אִיכָּא לְמִיפְרַךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the צד השוה built in step 23.
steps.kashyaTarget: The צד השוה from נגעים and שרצים.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Both sources share a strictness (spreading טומאה with less than a כזית) that a מת lacks, so their shared rule cannot be applied to אהל המת.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The entire צד השוה derivation from נגעים and שרצים (step 23).
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Both sources share a strictness that a מת lacks: they spread טומאה with less than a כזית. So their shared rule cannot be carried over to אהל המת.

steps.title: רבא from Barnish offers a new source
steps.stepSummary: After rejecting the derivation, רבא מברניש begins to give his own source. It continues on the next עמוד.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רבא מברניש said:
steps.whatsHappening: This line sets up the next move. רבא מברניש is about to give a new way to learn the rule, which continues on the next עמוד.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'אלא' signals that the previous derivation has been dropped. A completely different source is now coming.

phrases.english: Rather, Rava from Barnish said:
phrases.notes: His statement continues on the next עמוד.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After his challenge in step 24, רבא מברניש opens his own alternative derivation.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Introduces a new source (its content follows on the next amud).
